reuse.why: Routes all server paths, the preview and the API through one getExpectedAmount, reuses the rules module's getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and makes the existing getScheduledAmount delegate to it; a second entry point (getScheduledAmount with a positional op) remains alongside.

duplication.why: Removes the five inline midpoint copies (including schedule-template) in favour of one definition; the only overlap is the thin getScheduledAmount wrapper beside getExpectedAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the shared layer both server and client already import schedule amount logic from.

scope.why: Focused on amount resolution, its callers, API field, tests and release notes, though several comments now describe the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: One small, documented rule function; a maintainer must still remember to pass the op, and most client callers of getScheduledAmount do not.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every path that resolves an expected amount calls getExpectedAmount directly or through getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic remains; getScheduledAmount delegates to getExpectedAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained a third positional op parameter (callers pass a dummy false for inverse) and getExpectedAmount an op === 'isapprox' branch; client callers (SchedulesTable, mobile schedules, useScheduleEdit) call it without op, so the approximate rule silently does not apply there.
